doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Conservatory study and love of all music
summary: Asked about bebop, Allen says he studied clarinet with Delacluse at the conservatory and likes all music played from the heart.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: You could have decided at the time, after World War II bop was starting to become, you know, the way to play I guess. And you were associated a little bit with James Moody. Were you looking for something else besides bebop?
No, I was playing music, so I went to the conservatory and studied under Delacluse, the clarinetist and it was getting my technique up and classical music and everything. All music.
So I like all the music, because everything’s good when you listen when somebody’s playing it from the spirit and the heart you see.
That’s country music or blues, everything is from, you know real music. So I’m not prejudiced against the music, any kind.
